analysis: Reviewed .github/scripts/test-threat-budget.py: the base tail (lines 1084-1404) and the head start (lines 1-565). The only changed head range is 949-982, which adds three offline unit tests (manual GitHub rerun handoff, bounded runtime parsing, workload ceiling handoff). The patch excerpt is truncated and the changed lines fall outside the supplied head excerpt (which ends at line 565), so the test bodies were read from the patch only. The added tests assert fail-closed behavior: a rerun makes no paid calls and does not clear, runtime_seconds rejects invalid values and caps at 3000, and a workload limit hands off to human review without clearance. These tests run against synthetic local HTTP fixtures and use no real secrets. They do not touch the provider/coordinator runtime, the attestation or authorization paths, or the cache storage (T-041, TB-011, T-053). No threat-model assets (A-001 through A-017) or trust boundaries are affected. No production code changes are visible in this batch. The production implementations being tested (budget_runner, bedrock, threat-model-review.py runtime_seconds, merge_policy.clean) were not supplied, so the tests' correctness against them is unverified. Their consistency with the CI review gate is a question for other batches. No regression is identified here.
